sentences.text:
on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156368447/
1
The instant appeal has been filed challenging the finding on liability.

2. The first respondent filed a claim petition stating that while he was riding his two-wheeler, a vehicle insured with the appellant belonging to the second respondent herein came in the opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two-wheeler ridden by the first respondent, as a result of which the first respondent sustained grievous injuries.
3. The second respondent herein/owner of the vehicle remained ex parte before the Tribunal.

4. The appellant filed a counter stating that the accident took place only due to the negligence of the first respondent; and that the second respondent/insured did not have a valid licence and therefore,
they are not liable to pay any compensation.
_ _ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.
Before the Tribunal, the first respondent/claimant examined P.W. 1 and P.W.2 and marked Exs.P1 to P7.
The appellant examined R.W.1 and R.W.2 and marked Exs.R1 to R3.
The Disability Certificate was marked as Ex.C1.

Two other documents were marked as Exs.X1 and X2.
6.

The Tribunal, after taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence, held that the appellant had not established that the insured did not have a valid licence and hence, directed the appellant to pay the compensation.

7. The learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company submitted that the appellant is not liable to pay the compensation, since the rider of the insured vehicle/second respondent did not have a valid licence and in any event, the Tribunal ought to have given liberty to the appellant to pay and recover the compensation from the insured/second respondent.
8. Though notice has been sent to the second respondent, none has entered appearance.
_ _ _ _ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 9.
The only point for consideration in the instant appeal is whether the appellant is liable to pay compensation?
10. The appellant had stated in the counter before the Tribunal that the rider of the insured vehicle did not have a valid licence.
It was the case of the appellant before the Tribunal that the Police had also ascertained after the investigation that the rider of the insured vehicle did not have a valid licence.
However, the appellant had not produced any evidence to establish that the rider of the insured vehicle did not have a valid licence.
In such circumstances, it cannot be presumed that the rider did not have a valid licence.
Therefore, the finding of the Tribunal on this aspect cannot be faulted.
This Court is of the view that there is no infirmity in the award.
Hence, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is confirmed.

12. On such deposit, the first respondent/claimant is permitted to withdraw the award amount with interest and costs, less the amount already withdrawn, if any, by filing appropriate application before the Tribunal.
13. In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
